newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar mauls mark, Eurobourses have good day.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar mauls mark, Eurobourses have good day.

text.p: The dollar ended European trading looking robust on Tuesday, just below fresh 34-month peaks against the mark, and the bulls came out of hiding on European equity markets which closed around record levels.
Dealers said the dollar was well bid after U.S. new home sales jumped 8.6 percent in January, indicating an early interest rate hike might be needed to curb inflation.
"The new home sales were very strong...People are still thinking there is a good chance of the Fed (Federal Reserve) raising rates," said David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC James Capel.
Single-family home sales jumped 8.6 percent in January to an annual rate of 870,000 units against forecasts for a rise of 757,000 units.
The U.S. currency extended its gains to touch a fresh 34-month high of 1.7138 marks after the data. By the European close it was only just below that level against 1.6941 in late Europe on Monday.
Against the yen, the dollar touched session highs of 122.13 yen before settling at 121.95 yen, up from 120.92 in late dealings on Monday.
Dealers said profit-taking knocked the dollar lower with comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan possibly dampening the rally.
Greenspan's comments were seen as a mixed bag by traders. In prepared testimony to the House Budget Committee he said it was crucial to keep inflation down.
But he also said America's performance over the past year had been "quite favourable," with few signs of the imbalances that might have been expected late in this economic expansion.

One factor behind the dollar's strength was a key U.S. economic forecasting gauge, which posted its largest increase in eight months in January, suggesting economic growth will accelerate during the first half of the year.

The Conference Board said its index of leading indicators -- designed to forecast economic activity six to nine months ahead -- rose 0.3 percent in January after a 0.1 percent gain in December. The January increase was the largest since a 0.3 percent rise last May. During the six months ended in January, the index increased 0.7 percent.

On the bourses almost flat early trading on Wall Street added little direction to a bullish day. Major European centres opened sharply higher, kickstarted by New York's higher close on Monday -- which ended a Wall Street's three session decline.
London's FTSE 100 share index ended at a new record close but fell short of its all-time high as a dithering Dow took the steam out of a strong early rally in British blue-chips.
The FTSE closed 50.6 points higher at 4,357.7, just beating the previous closing high set on February 19.
It failed to breach its trading peak of 4,362.4 after being stopped in its tracks just below the 4,360 level when an expected helping hand from the Dow failed to materialise.
"It was a very good day but Wall Street just didn't help us enough to take us to a new record," one dealer said.

In Germany both the Dax index of floor trading and the IBIS DAX electronic index closed at record highs, pushed up by the dollar and an earlier surge in German car stocks following a wave of positive news from the Geneva carshow.

On the Paris bouse French shares also staged a strong rally, helped by the dollar and bullish underlying sentiment, and closed a whisper away from their all-time high reached on February 18 of this year.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended up 51.43 points or 1.98 percent at 2,651.69.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7135 marks and 121.90 yen, compared with 1.6941 and 120.92 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 50.6 points at 4,357.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 51.43 points at 2,651.69.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 56.8 points at 3,320.66. In later screen-based trading the IBIS DAX closed up 86 points at 3,345.09.
PRECIOUS METALS Gold closed at $360.00 compared with London's previous close of $362.25.
